entities.label: Institution
entities.summary:
A-Ma Temple (Mazu Temple, Temple of Matsu) in Macau is the oldest and most famous temple in Macau, dedicated to the goddess Mazu (A-Ma), the patroness of fishermen and sailors. Built around 1488 CE — predating Portuguese colonization of Macau — it is a complex of several pavilions, gates, and shrines climbing up a rocky hillside near the Inner Harbour, and is believed to have given Macau its name.

According to legend, 'Macau' derives from 'A-Ma Gao' (Bay of A-Ma): when Portuguese sailors arrived in 1557 and asked local fishermen the name of the place, they pointed to the temple and said 'A-Ma Gao,' which the Portuguese misheard as 'Macao.' The temple's connection to Portuguese discovery of Macau makes it the symbolic starting point of the city's hybrid Chinese-Portuguese history.

The temple complex consists of four pavilions built at different times: the Gate Pavilion (most ancient), the Prayer Hall, the Hall of Benevolence, and the Hall of Guanyin. Visitors and fishermen come to pray for safe sea voyages — the temple's maritime protection function remains active today, with incense smoke perpetually rising from its urns. Designated a UNESCO World Heritage site as part of the Historic Centre of Macau in 2005, A-Ma Temple represents the religious heart of Macanese Chinese culture.
